jobs.text: The Sundarbans covers about 10,000 square kilometres across Bangladesh and India, with the larger part in Bangladesh. The mangrove trees have breathing roots that stick up from the mud like pencils, and they protect the coast from storm surges. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and the Royal Bengal tiger is its most famous resident.

Balancing income against the environment is a live debate.

jobs.text: The name Shat Gombuj means “sixty domes”, although the mosque has many more domes than that; some say the name comes from its sixty pillars. It was built in the fifteenth century in the time of Khan Jahan Ali, a governor and saint who also dug ponds and built roads around Bagerhat. Thick brick walls keep the prayer hall cool, and Bagerhat joined the UNESCO World Heritage list in 1985.
